title: Dubai Off-Plan Market: Correction or Crash? The Numbers and My Forecast
seoTitle: Dubai Off-Plan Market: Correction or Crash?
description: Dubai home sales fell 38% in Q3 and prices sit about 10% below their peak. The numbers, the 2027 supply question, and my forecast for buyers and developers.
answer: Dubai is in a correction, not a crash. Q3 sales fell about 38% and prices are roughly 10% below their February peak, hitting apartments harder than villas. Off-plan is still 72% of sales. A large supply wave in 2027 is the real test; my view is the market finds its floor in 2027.
body:
For four years Dubai was not running, it was sprinting: record sales, record prices, record launches every quarter. Then, at the end of February, conflict broke out in the region and the market had to stop and catch its breath. Here is the full picture, with the figures reported at the time of recording, and my own forecast at the end.

## The numbers

- **Q3 sales:** about 34,000 homes, roughly **38% fewer** than the same quarter last year.
- **Q3 value:** about AED 72 billion, down **47%**.
- **September:** sales down more than 40% year over year.
- **Off-plan share:** even now, about **72%** of homes sold in Dubai were off-plan.

Buyers did not disappear. They became more careful.

## Prices: a split market

According to the ValuStrat index, prices peaked in February. By August they were about 10% below that peak and about 3% lower than a year earlier. The split matters: apartments are down more than 5% year over year, villas less than 2%. S&P Global's rating agency work puts the fall at 5% to 15% since the end of last year, depending on the area.

That is a correction, not a crash, and it is hitting apartments much harder than villas.

## The supply question

Dubai delivered almost 25,000 new homes in the first half of the year, with many more scheduled before year end. For 2027, estimates range from about 62,000 units to more than 160,000. That is not a forecast, it is a range wide enough to drive a truck through. The reason is that in Dubai, scheduled and delivered are two different things: delays and phased handovers are normal.

Even so, a lot of keys are coming, and each one is an apartment looking for a buyer or a tenant. The good news is that developers saw it coming. Apartment launches in the first half fell by about 58% compared with last year.

## Two opposite developer strategies

Some developers are fighting for every buyer with discounts of 20%, in some cases reportedly up to 50%, according to Emaar's founder Mohamed Alabbar. The strongest developers are doing the opposite: Emaar says it does not discount, and it announced an AED 200 billion megaproject in the middle of the downturn. Same city, same buyers, opposite strategies. The weak sell at a discount. The strong buy the future.

## What the experts say

- **S&P Global** expects a gradual correction, not a sudden fall, with more investors selling on the secondary market.
- **UBS** ranks Dubai fourth of 23 cities for housing bubble risk, but says that risk eased this year as the boom slowed, and calls Dubai one of the more affordable major cities in its study.
- **Mohamed Alabbar** expects a 5% to 10% adjustment, then a healthier balance in 2027.

## My forecast

This is my opinion, not financial advice.

- **Next six months:** sales stay low; prices move sideways or slide, especially apartments in areas with the most new supply. More developers offer discounts and longer payment plans.
- **2027 is the real test.** As keys arrive, investors who planned to flip at handover will face more competition than expected, with more units on the secondary market and pressure on rents. I expect apartment prices to keep correcting through 2027. Villas and prime locations should hold up better.
- **The wild card is geopolitics.** Real stability could bring the market back faster than most expect. A deeper conflict means a deeper, longer correction.

My call: a correction, not a collapse. 2027 is when the market finds its floor, and for patient buyers the window opens between late 2027 and 2028.

## What it means for developers

The era of selling on hype is over, at least for now. When a market sprints, buyers take anything. When it catches its breath, they ask questions: is this project real, will it be delivered, what exactly am I buying? The developers who answer clearly will keep selling. The others will have to discount.
takeaways: Q3 sales fell about 38%, but off-plan still made up about 72% of Dubai purchases.
Prices are roughly 10% below the February peak; apartments are falling faster than villas.
2027 deliveries are estimated anywhere from about 62,000 to over 160,000 units.
Weaker developers are discounting while the strongest are launching new megaprojects.
My forecast: correction, not collapse, with a floor in 2027 and a window for patient buyers in late 2027 to 2028.
faq: Is the Dubai property market crashing?
The figures point to a correction rather than a crash: prices are about 10% below their peak, with apartments falling faster than villas, and buyers are still active.
Is now a good time to buy off-plan in Dubai?

In my view patient buyers have more to gain by waiting, as 2027 supply is likely to push apartment prices lower. Villas and prime locations are more resilient. This is an opinion, not financial advice.
Why are 2027 supply forecasts for Dubai so different?
Because scheduled completions and actual deliveries differ a lot in Dubai; projects are often delayed or handed over in phases.
What should Dubai developers do in a correction?
Give buyers certainty: clear information about the exact unit, delivery and track record. Without it, discounts become the only lever.
